parties:
Habibullah, Director of National Bank Limited and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Bangladesh Bank and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 50. There is no allegation that NCL granted the waiver of interest or condition of fulfillment of some conditions and on such fulfillment of such conditions the waiver was allowed. Petitioner''s allegation is that on 26-4-92 interest of Taka 38,40,043.00 was waived by the bank by crediting the same in the statement of account of Subarna Trading Company Ltd. and the said amount was again debited in the said account on 4-5-92 (vide Annexure-E). There is nothing to show who granted the said waiver and under what authority. Only supporting document is the copies of bank''s statement of accounts Annexure-E which shows that in the entry dated 25-4-92 aforesaid amount was credited "By Nan S/L" but before the said entry is a cross mark and by the immediate next entry dated 4-5-92 aforesaid amount was debited, By A/D IMW reversed." Aforesaid words quoted above have not been explained to us. However, from the nature of the entry, reversal of the entry within 8 days and specially cross mark before the entry crediting the amount show that the same was wholly unauthorised and made by way of manoeuvering through same interested persons. In such circumstances and in the absence of petitioner''s doing anything, in pursuance of any promise by the NCL there is no question of application of the doctrine of promissory estoppel.
